title: UI and viewport scale become incorrect when using Stretch (any mode) across monitors with different DPI scaling
body: ### Tested versions Godot 4.5 stable ### System information Godot v4.5.stable - Windows 11 - Multi-window, 2 monitors - NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 Laptop (Driver 566.26, DCH) - OpenGL(Compatibility) - AMD Ryzen 7 7735HS with Radeon Graphics (3.20 GHz) - ### Issue description When using multiple monitors with different DPI scaling factors (for example, one at 125% and another at 100%), any project that has Stretch enabled (`viewport `or `canvas_items` mode) will cause the UI and viewport scale to become distorted or offset after moving the editor or the running game window between screens. **Stretch disabled:** **Stretch canvas_items:** The issue occurs consistently — even if `Allow hiDPI `is disabled. Once the distortion happens, it persists across restarts, even if: - Cache is cleared - Godot is reinstalled - System is rebooted - Running a copy of the project Only setting Stretch → Mode to disabled prevents the problem, but this also disables all automatic resizing and scaling behavior. ### Steps to reproduce I can no longer reliably reproduce this issue in new projects after rebooting the system, but my current project remains broken and continues to show the incorrect UI and viewport scaling behavior. Possible reproduction steps: 1. Use a multi-monitor setup with different DPI scaling (e.g., main monitor 125%, secondary 100%). 2. Create a new project with any Control-based UI. 3. In Project Settings → Display → Window: - Set Stretch → Mode to viewport (or canvas_items) - Set Stretch → Aspect to expand - Optionally disable Allow HiDPI 4. Run the project on the 125% screen. With the embedded game and floating workspace options checked in the Game tab. 5. Drag the running game window to the 100% screen. 6. Change the game size settings in the Game tab 7. Observe the following: - UI becomes misaligned, offset, or scaled incorrectly. - Returning to the original monitor does not fix it. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [animalpuzzle_mrp.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22705951/animalpuzzle_mrp.zip)
